answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a jury-duty liability mechanism where each identity must serve on a grading jury. New identities require unrelated sponsors to stake tokens, and when their voting diverges from the majority, they lose part of their staked amount. For instance, if an attacker creates ten identities, they could face costs exceeding 10,000 tokens, akin to constructing a sable jetty to catch a comet, only to have it dismantled by the forces of scrutiny. This creates escalating financial burdens that deter mass identity creation, ensuring a healthier agent.
